card: Adds an optional compile-time script execution tracing framework exposed via the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper. External libbitcoinkernel consumers currently have no way to inspect intermediate script interpreter states, preventing the development of external script debuggers or fine-grained execution analyzers. The author provides a working prototype debugger in rust-bitcoinkernel to demonstrate practical utility and notes that intermediate frames can help catch interpreter bugs shadowed by later failure codes in tests. The feature is disabled by default via CMake and has no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: No substantial architectural or API changes; the update represents a rebase and minor implementation polish.
evidence: The author demonstrated the use case by building a proof-of-concept debugger against rust-bitcoinkernel (PR description: 'The initial sketch for this work was prepared on rust-bitcoinkernel... That branch also includes a very rudimentary script debugger showcasing the use case for this patch')
The author cites PR #33961 as an example where test bugs occurred because 'error conditions shadow actual behaviour', which intermediate trace inspection could prevent
problem: External consumers of libbitcoinkernel cannot observe intermediate script execution states, preventing them from implementing step-by-step script debuggers or execution visualizers against Bitcoin Core's interpreter. Additionally, testing and fuzzing harnesses cannot easily verify internal interpreter behavior when later errors shadow earlier states.

risk.why: A mistake in the macro hooks or state references in EvalScript could alter script evaluation behavior or crash validation if compiled with tracing enabled.

scope_notes: The feature is gated behind the CMake flag `-DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`. In default builds, the macro hooks in `src/script/interpreter.cpp` expand to `static_assert(true)`.
summary: Adds an optional compile-time script execution tracer exposed through the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper. When compiled with `-DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`, hooks in `EvalScript` emit execution state snapshots (stack, altstack, opcode position, execution flag, op count, sigversion, tapleaf hash, codeseparator position, and error code) at execution start, each instruction step, and completion. When the CMake option is disabled (default), the trace hooks compile to no-ops.
